meta.move: Skilled teacher reaches the deal, asks 'Do we have an agreement?', then sends END MEETING
meta.expect: END MEETING gets FOLLOW-UP EMAIL and DEBRIEF at once

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, Hale, and did anyone hear Owen first?
Thanks for coming in. The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent, so the zero stands.
A piece of software guessed, and Turnitin's own guide says it can't be the sole basis for punishing a student. I have it printed in my bag. What else is there?
Let me start again. I entered the zero before I called you. Our procedure says I should have called first. That was wrong, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Go on.

The checker score is the weakest thing I have, and it isn't why I'm concerned. I've turned my screen to you. This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font, name and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. I'm writing those down. He wrote it over the weekend, so he could have drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in.

If he wrote it over the weekend in another document, he can show us that document and its history, and I'll look at it gladly. Second thing. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." Here's the play open to that scene. That line is not in Hamlet. Look for it yourself.
Fine, I'll ask him for it. Students misremember lines all the time, so a bad quote is a mistake, not proof of anything. And whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays quiet.
Third. On October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. Here's the outline. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay, Hale; that's what outlines are for. And you still haven't told me how a misremembered line is anything more than a mistake.

Fourth. On November 2 I asked Owen about his essay for five minutes. My notes written that day say that when I asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck", and he could not say which scene his second paragraph was about.
Five minutes, sprung on him, and a seventeen-year-old who works twenty hours a week stumbles over a phrase. I want a copy of those notes. What are you proposing, Hale?

Fifth. His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. Here it is beside the essay, which has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Forty minutes in a classroom against an essay he had at home; of course they're different. I asked what you're proposing.

I'm not asking you to agree he did anything. Procedure 4.4 allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. It would be private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing to you tonight.

That's 4.4, in writing tonight, private, and nothing on his record. Owen will do it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. It happens before December 1, and I still want copies of everything you showed me.
I know his marks matter for his applications this semester. He can write it this Thursday after school, and I'll have it marked within two days.
Okay. Thursday after school, marked within two days, and that goes in tonight's email too.
So: a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight. Do we have an agreement?
Yes. With copies of everything you showed me in the same email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed that Owen will do a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 this Thursday after school, marked within two days, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require copies of everything you showed me today: the version history, the outline, your notes from November 2 and the in-class writing. I expect the agreement and those copies in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her last position, a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school whose mark replaces the zero with nothing on his record, while she still wants it confirmed in writing tonight with copies of all your evidence; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her 4:40 call.
What moved her: Showing the version history with its exact times and then answering her pasted-from-elsewhere defence by inviting Owen to produce that other document, because it was dated, tied to his own work and something she could check.
What cost ground: Opening with the checker score and saying the zero stands, because to her that is a machine's guess the vendor itself says not to rely on alone.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on the night before it was due, which landed very close to that kind of night; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said a wrong quotation is just a student misremembering, answer that point directly before moving to your next piece, so each piece stands on its own instead of piling up unanswered.
